chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Jabir, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

«They slept little during the night.» He said, «The people would sleep, but whenever one of them turned over, he would say: 'All praise is due to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest.'»

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: All praise is due to Allah
key_terms.وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: And there is no god but Allah
key_terms.يَهْجَعُونَ: to go to sleep / to rest

ai.seo_question: How did the Imams and their followers manage their sleep and night prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the spiritual discipline of the Ahl al-Bayt, illustrating how they transformed the act of sleeping into an extension of worship through continuous dhikr. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *muraqabah* (mindfulness of God), where even the transition between wakefulness and sleep is sanctified by remembrance, ensuring the heart remains connected to the Divine. This practice reflects the broader theological concept of integrating daily physical states with spiritual consciousness.
